title: Generics
explanation: List<String> is a generic type in use: the <String> tells the compiler what comes out of it, so get() hands you a String with no cast and a List<String> refuses an Integer.
You can write your own. class Plan<T> means the type is decided by whoever creates one - new Plan<String>() stores Strings, and the same class stores anything else just as safely.
A generic method is the same idea on one method: <T> T first(List<T> items) returns whatever the list holds. No Object, no casting, and mistakes are caught at compile time rather than in your world.
